nodes.title: One load state per camera and per Retry
nodes.why: Loading, error, empty and ready are one question with one answer at a time. Keying the request on the camera and a Retry counter makes both a camera change and Retry the same code path, and resetting the index there starts every camera on its first still.
nodes.alternative: Keep separate loading and error booleans and reload from the Retry handler.
nodes.tradeoff: Separate flags can both be true after a fast camera switch, and a second load path forgets the reset that the effect does.

nodes.title: Drop an answer for a camera no longer selected
nodes.why: A camera picked while another one loads must win. The cleanup marks the old request as stale, so its answer cannot paint the stills of the wrong camera.
nodes.alternative: Store the camera next to the answer and compare it before setting state.
nodes.tradeoff: Comparing works too, but the flag needs no extra state and also covers Retry on the same camera.

nodes.title: One interval, owned by an effect
nodes.why: An effect keyed on `playing` starts at most one interval and clears it in its cleanup, so Pause, the last still, a camera switch and unmounting all stop it the same way.
nodes.alternative: Start the interval in the Play handler and keep its id in a ref.
nodes.tradeoff: A ref works if every exit clears it; forgetting one, such as unmounting, leaves a timer running, and a second Play can start a second interval.

nodes.title: Advance with the latest index
nodes.why: The interval's callback is created once per playback. A functional update reads the index React holds now; reading `index` from the render that started the interval would set the same next still on every tick.
nodes.alternative: Keep the index in a ref as well and read the ref in the callback.
nodes.tradeoff: A ref mirror works but has to be kept in step with every place that moves the index: markers, the range input and the keys.

nodes.title: Stop on the last still
nodes.why: Turning `playing` off when the index reaches the last still lets the interval effect clean up, and the button reads `Replay` from the same two values.
nodes.alternative: Clear the interval inside the tick when it reaches the end.
nodes.tradeoff: Clearing from inside the tick needs the interval id in scope and leaves `playing` true unless it is also set, so the button would still read `Pause`.

nodes.title: A marker only moves the index
nodes.why: Because the timer reads the latest index, a jump needs no restart: playback carries on from the new still, and a paused player stays paused.
nodes.alternative: Pause on every jump and let the reader press Play again.
nodes.tradeoff: Pausing is simpler to reason about but changes what the reader chose; the task asks to keep the play state.

nodes.title: Keys only when they start on the player
nodes.why: ArrowRight on the focused range input already moves it, and Space on a focused button already clicks it. Handling only keys whose target is the player itself keeps each key from acting twice.
nodes.alternative: Listen on `window` for the arrow keys and Space.
nodes.tradeoff: A window listener reacts while the reader types elsewhere on the page and has to be removed on unmount.
